metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast (especially after sharp drops), so reduce forecast peak by 5–15% in early horizon.
- After a strong upward spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting downward; apply a 3–7 day lag correction to avoid over-optimism.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- In high-sentiment (positive) periods, model often under-forecasts volatility; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for 3–5 day horizon.
- If true outcome shows sharp reversal after 10–15 day forecast, model tends to miss it; apply 2–5 day “reversal buffer” to forecast tail.
